APPLICATION 01 / INSPECT

Industrial Underwater Inspection ROVs

Make submerged condition visible.

Choose an ROV around the inspection result you need, then work back through visibility, access, depth and sensor requirements.

Home / Applications / Industrial underwater inspection

Who this is for

Inspection contractors, water utilities and hydropower maintenance teams.

Project inputs

  • Structure drawings and inspection objectives
  • Depth, current and expected visibility
  • Access dimensions and launch location
  • Required sensors, data formats and reporting criteria
Build a project brief

The short answer

An industrial underwater inspection ROV replaces diver inspection of intakes, dams and submerged structures with a remotely operated camera and sensor platform. Choose it around the result you need: the R-30 for compact visual work, the R-45 when sonar, positioning or tools add payload.

01

Start with the inspection objective

Documenting general condition, locating a defect and measuring its extent are different tasks. Define the structure, required coverage, reporting format and acceptance criteria before comparing vehicles.

02

Let visibility guide the sensing package

An optical camera provides interpretable detail when water clarity and lighting permit. Imaging sonar may help navigation and feature recognition in poor visibility. Neither automatically supplies survey-grade dimensions or a complete defect assessment.

03

Match the vehicle to the site

Compare working depth, currents, smallest access opening, vehicle clearance and deployment space. The R-30 and R-45 have different size and payload allowances. Evaluate them with the actual sensors installed.

04

Plan the complete field system

Account for the control station, tether, reel, power supply, launch method and recovery equipment. A vehicle specification alone does not describe the staffing, transport or infrastructure needed for a mission.

05

Define usable outputs

Specify video recording, time references, position references and annotations. Confirm which files can be exported and how observations will be connected to the asset owner’s reporting workflow.

BEFORE YOU SPECIFY

Frequently asked questions.

Which ROV should I choose?

Start with the payload, access and site conditions. The R-30 has a brochure payload of 3 kg; the R-45 has 8 kg. The complete integrated package still needs review.

Can it inspect without visibility?

A suitable sonar can provide useful information in low visibility, but it is a separate sensing choice. Define what the mission must detect and verify that the proposed package can do it.
